title: Replace date_utils_test.dart's real DateTime.now() read with a fixed/injected clock
why: This is the only wall-clock read across all 14 test files in the batch — every other test in the suite (and in the file's own source, date_utils.dart, which is explicitly designed around a swappable LocalDayClock so "day-boundary semantics are deterministic in tests") uses fixed DateTime.utc(...) literals. Comparing DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() against a freshly-read DateTime.now() with a 1-second tolerance is a live flake source: any CI scheduling jitter, GC pause, or slow VM startup between the two calls pushes the gap over 1 second and fails the test for a reason unrelated to the code under test.
recommendation: Override the LocalDayClock with a fixed fake instant (per the source file's own documented pattern: `localDayClockProvider.overrideWithValue(...)` or `useLocalDayClock`) and assert DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() returns exactly that fixed instant, rather than "close to real time".
acceptance_criteria: The nowUtc test asserts equality against an injected/fixed clock value, not a real-time tolerance window.
